rows.t: Mid-century Brass Rooster

det.desc: Decorative brass animal figurines gained immense popularity during the mid-20th century, particularly within Hollywood Regency and transitional interior design schemes. Artisans often utilized lost-wax or sand-casting techniques to achieve highly textured surfaces that caught the light and added dramatic flair to home decor. Roosters, symbolizing vigilance and courage, were frequently cast as paired fighting or strutting display pieces for dining rooms and entryways. Many of these expressive brass sculptures were produced in European foundries, notably in Italy and parts of Spain, before being exported to American department stores and interior design boutiques. The rich patinas and meticulous feather detailing reflect a period when heavy, sculptural brass accessories were a hallmark of sophisticated interior styling. Over the decades, these charming decorative animals have transitioned from mainstream home furnishings into sought-after vintage collectibles. 11” at tallest 6 1/2” at widest
